content.title: Delete an existing task by clicking its x control
content.intent: Prove that clicking a task's "x" control removes that existing task from the todo list.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning with one representative valid action class: deleting one existing task through its per-task "x" control. Reused the existing add-task scenario as setup precondition instead of minting duplicate setup coverage. Reviewed negative, boundary, security, and a11y techniques but did not mint separate scenarios because the current source only asserts the direct happy-path delete action and does not define confirmation, invalid delete attempts, alternate activations, or protected access semantics. No covering array was needed because this path has one grounded action dimension and one asserted outcome.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applied equivalence partitioning because the PRD defines one valid delete trigger — clicking the task's "x" control — and no outcome-changing input classes beyond the existence of a task to delete.
[applicability] Did not apply boundary value analysis because the cited source defines no numeric, ordered, or length-constrained delete input.
[applicability] Did not mint a negative scenario because the PRD does not specify behavior for absent tasks, confirmation prompts, undo, blocked deletes, or delete failures.
[applicability] Did not mint security or auth scenarios because the source does not place deletion behind login, roles, or cross-user access boundaries.
